item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports content-aware recommendation, but does not establish gains for the exact constraint: one BERT4Rec trained from scratch using only local titles/descriptions. [The Elephant in the Room (RecSys 2024)](https://github.com/777pomingzi/Rethinking-PLM-in-RS) enhances BERT4Rec by initializing item embeddings from a behavior-tuned language model; this uses pretrained representations and staged training. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) learns from flattened item metadata using masked latent-representation prediction and two-stage training. Useful architectural inspiration, but its results do not demonstrate that a small local lexical encoder will reproduce those gains. [FineRec (2024)](https://www.atailab.cn/seminar2024Spring/pdf/2024_ISGIR_FineRec-Exploring%20Fine-grained%20Sequential%20Recommendation.pdf) extracts attribute–opinion pairs using an LLM and reviews; those inputs are unavailable here.\n\nTraining cost and optimization interference matter. [DeCoRec (2025)](https://cwang-zju.github.io/files/mm25.pdf) reports that ID embeddings and modality representations converge at different rates, with naïve fusion sometimes reducing accuracy. A constraint-compatible hypothesis is therefore a small, randomly initialized token/subword embedding pool over titles and truncated descriptions, projected into the item-ID embedding and jointly trained within one BERT4Rec, using the same fused item representation in its single scoring head. This is an experimental inference, not a verified literature result. Preserve model numbers, units and lexical phrases that could identify compatibility or specifications; first measure metadata coverage, missingness and distinguishing-token frequency. Titles/descriptions may expose functional relationships, but their actual availability remains unverified. Compare macro validation HR@10 and GPU time against the corrected baseline before investing in a larger text Transformer."}
